chunks: What the Shaykh — may Allah the Exalted support him — informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from 'Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), that he said:

A junub must not touch a dirham or a dinar upon which the name of Allah is inscribed; must not perform istinja' while wearing a ring bearing the name of Allah; must not engage in sexual intercourse while wearing it; and must not enter the toilet while wearing it.

key_terms.اَلْجُنُبُ: person in a state of janaba (major ritual impurity requiring ghusl)
key_terms.يَسْتَنْجِي: performs istinja' (cleanses oneself after relieving oneself)

ai.seo_question: What are the prohibitions for a junub regarding coins and rings bearing the name of Allah, according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS)?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) enumerates four prohibitions incumbent upon a person in a state of janaba: touching a dirham or dinar bearing the name of Allah inscribed upon it; performing istinja' while wearing a ring on which Allah's name is engraved; engaging in sexual intercourse while wearing it; and entering the toilet while wearing it. These rulings reflect the Shia jurisprudential principle that the divine name must be shielded from defilement and dishonour in all contexts, whether of ritual impurity or intimate acts.
